q1_issues.issue: The rule's PREMISE is built out of Skolem-function terms ((Member (sk_block $c) block), (Agent (sk_block $c) cliff_spire), (Theme (sk_block $c) $c), (Source (sk_block $c) north_wind)), which the instruction set forbids outright — "a premise never contains a Skolem term" — so nothing can ever match it and the rule is permanently inert.

"blocked FROM the north wind" names what is warded off, not a spatial origin, so it answers none of where/when/how/whence/whither and should take the preposition-named oblique; Source asserts the north wind as the blocking event's origin.

The consequent nests a whole (Implication (PartOf $x ...) ...) inside another rule's conclusion, with its own free $x — per-member distribution rules are emitted at top level (or as a sealed sibling inside a seal), never as a conjunct of another rule's consequent.

q2_gaps: a definite plural subject that is itself introduced inside a whenever-rule's CONSEQUENT ("the lanterns in that cove") and needs per-member distribution of a copular/state predicate — the instruction set gives the distribution rule only at top level or inside a seal, never nested in a consequent

durative "through <period>" ("stay lit through winter") — During is restricted to during/while/throughout with a reified outer eventuality, no interval Start/End or duration measure is stated, and no head covers "through"
notes: The compound decompositions (cliff_spire genus with the noun modifier suppressed; north_wind genus plus its cardinal modifier) and the stay-lit continuation-copular shape (reified state + Still + flat atom, no tense) are all correct. "through winter" lands on (Time e winter), which under-specifies rather than misstates; separately, definite "the north wind" and bare-plural "cliff-spires" are used as bare kind constants in role-filler slots, which I read as borderline rather than clearly wrong inside a generic rule.
